results.response: Two axes: clever-vs-stupid and lazy-vs-industrious. Four quadrants. Clever-lazy is the target — efficient, finds the structural fix, doesn't burn cycles. results.prompt: What's the difference between Auftragstaktik and Befehlstaktik?
results.response:
Both are staff-planning models, but they differ in execution discipline. Befehlstaktik is top-down, rigid, and command-driven: superiors issue detailed instructions; subordinates execute without deviation. It ensures precise coordination when communications channels are clear and frictionless.

Auftragstaktik is bottom-up, risk-accepting, and mission-driven: commanders assign missions with broad parameters; subordinates determine their own execution paths to achieve the objective. It preserves initiative at lower levels but requires trusted, autonomous operators who understand the larger strategy.

The structural difference is control vs. trust. Befehlstaktik centralizes it with command; Auftragstaktik distributes it to the front line. The operational cost of Auftragstaktik only pays off when the force has high reliability and clear situational awareness. In fog or friction, rigid Befehlstaktik preserves discipline but risks paralysis; flexible Auftragstaktik risks fragmentation.

Practically, this means Befehlstaktik is easier to staff and audit because it tracks compliance. Auftragstaktik requires continuous verification that local decisions align with the overall objective—otherwise the mission drifts. The German army standardized on Auftragstaktik after World War I because centralized planning was actively costing them ground; they shifted command authority down to preserve operational velocity where communications were poor.

Both models exist in your stack (gs-geoserver, Ollama, mission-budget). gs-geoserver is Befehlstaktik: detailed configuration, explicit validation gates. Ollama/Ayush are Auftragstaktik at the agent layer—take the instruction, work it out, report progress without waiting for further hand-holding. The mission-budget system (clever-lazy by design) is also Auftragstaktik: trust the allocation algorithm to distribute risk and capacity efficiently across projects.

Default mode for Ray's operational planning: Auftragstaktik. The operator sets the objective; the system works out the execution. The structural fix is trusting the local decision-maker with the authority to fail fast without penalty, as long as they stay within the mission parameters.

Continued is the right default. Cheaper, faster, and the v0.1 teacher

generalizing the discrimination layer. Verify by running a blind
eval on the new pairs against v0.1 versus v0.1 retrained: if both
score roughly the same on the new signals, continued wins.

Call it and run the eval before committing the pipeline.
